author: BeauHD
description: A federal bankruptcy judge has approved Google's $10 million purchase of internal business data from defunct Spirit Airlines during a hearing on Tuesday. Reuters reports: US Bankruptcy Judge Sean Lane, ruling from the bench, cleared the deal after Alphabet's Google agreed last week to implement additional privacy protections for the data, following concerns from labor unions and more than 120 US lawmakers. Discount carrier Spirit halted operations in May. As part of its closure and asset liquidation, Google won an auction in August for employee data from emails, spreadsheets and calendars, as well as for marketing, productivity and operations. Google has said it plans to use the data for product development and AI training.
title: US Bankruptcy Judge Approves Spirit Airlines Data Sale to Google

author: BeauHD
description:
Best Buy has resumed selling Blu-ray movies directly through its website and physical stores after exiting the physical media business in 2023. The retailer currently offers a limited selection of 15 Blu-ray listings, including new releases like The Odyssey and Project Hail Mary and older titles like It's a Wonderful Life (1943), Saving Private Ryan (1998), and The Godfather (1972). Ars Technica reports: Overall, the sales of Blu-rays and DVDs in the US have been steadily declining, and annual consumer spending dropped 9.3 percent from 2024 to 2025, according to the Digital Entertainment Group (DEG). During this same time, however, consumer spending on 4K Blu-ray discs specifically increased 12 percent year over year, per DEG.
 "We're seeing a lot of evidence, including at the Criterion Mobile Closet, that more young people are thinking about physical media in a different way," Peter Becker, president of Criterion, which sells Blu-rays and DVDs online, told the Los Angeles Times in Fe
title: Best Buy Resumes Blu-ray Sales

author: BeauHD
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Washington Sun: Wall Street executives and the National Security Agency have told members of Congress that this week's widespread tech outages were caused by attempts to fix vulnerabilities identified by artificial intelligence, according to three sources familiar with the private conversations. [...] "These models are identifying massive vulnerabilities, and that increases the urgency to patch right away," said one congressional official briefed on the matter. "They're trying to push through a lot of patches all at once -- more than the system was designed for."
 
On Monday, banks such as JP Morgan Chase blamed software-related bugs for the service issues. On Tuesday, the NSA said that "scheduled routine maintenance" was responsible for the "temporary degradation" of some of its networks. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told CNBC on Tuesday that "they're pushing new technology on top of really old computer systems, and it j
title: Bank CEOs, NSA Tell Congress That AI-Driven Patches Are Behind Outages

author: BeauHD
description: Longtime Slashdot reader HnT writes: Security researchers at Calif have disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a critical 9.2-rated memory-corruption bug in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder. By sending a malformed string ending in a stray = character, attackers can trigger an out-of-bounds heap write to leak sensitive memory or achieve pre-auth remote code execution on major platforms like Jira, Jenkins, and Keycloak. Although Calif says the vulnerability is difficult to exploit, Oracle released a critical patch update Tuesday, and CISA urged organizations to update immediately. OpenJDK's security advisory can be found here. The Calif researchers warned that vulnerable systems could remain exposed for five to 10 years, given how slowly some organizations patch their infrastructure.
title: 'Java4Shell' Flaw Exposes OpenJDK to RCE via Base64

author: BeauHD
description: Cambridge Dictionary has named "human" its 2026 Word of the Year, reflecting growing concerns about artificial intelligence and its impact on what it means to be human. "AI is changing how we talk about being human," said Colin McIntosh, the dictionary's lexicographer. "Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children." The Associated Press reports: The adjective derived from the Latin "humanus" and in use since the 1450s is defined by Cambridge as "having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines." [...] Other word contenders for 2026 included "agent," for an AI system that can make decisions and operate without human control and "analogue" for experiences or objects not involving the internet or digital technology.
title: Cambridge Dictionary Names 'Human' Its 2026 Word of the Year

author: BeauHD
description: Waymo has temporarily suspended freeway operations across all its robotaxi markets after California regulators ordered the company off the state's highways over repeated incidents involving construction zones. The restriction follows a June recall (PDF) of nearly 3,800 vehicles and subsequent software updates (PDF) that failed to prevent further incidents, including a robotaxi driving past a California Highway Patrol rolling roadblock. Ars Technica reports: "Safety is at the foundation of everything we do," Waymo told Ars. "Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, servi
title: Waymo Robotaxis Pulled From Freeways Indefinitely

author: BeauHD
description:
Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia could weaken the open AI model ecosystem he spent years championing, potentially strengthening closed-model developers like OpenAI and Anthropic, according to the Financial Times. From the report: The US chip giant's former chief threw Nvidia's balance sheet into creating a broad AI ecosystem, including by seeding and acquiring start-ups involved in the development of open-source and open-weight models, which users can customize and run on their own hardware. Huang was a forceful advocate for their spread, lobbying against Washington's moves to restrict the use of Chinese-made open models while seeking the development of US alternatives. "Our AI leadership will be judged not by one frontier AI model, but by whether the United States builds a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses into every sector," he wrote this summer in his first-ever message on X.
 
His ignominious exit from Nvidia deprives the open model sector of its most vocal and influential
title: Jensen Huang's Fall Hits 'Open' Models In Boost to Anthropic and OpenAI

author: BeauHD
description: An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Verge: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he's AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. "I am AGI-pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy's organization around AGI?" he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco. But Nadella doesn't think frontier models like Claude are conscious. "I don't think so," he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman's view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic's team has "wireheaded" themselves, and that this approach is dangerous. Nadella wasn't quite as firm about it. "It's a good debate," he said. "I'm not sort of dogmatic
title: Satya Nadella Says He's AGI-Pilled Now

author: BeauHD
description:
NASA's Voyager 1 has become the first human-made object to travel one light-day from Earth, or 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers). This means radio signals will take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft, now nearly 50 years into its mission. "Since light is essentially the maximum speed in the universe (absent using devices like wormholes, or quantum-physics puzzles), it's a big deal -- so big that NASA will be celebrating the milestone by asking fans to shine Morse Code signals at the sky," reports Space.com. From the report: But why will Voyager 2 take nearly a decade longer? It comes down to choices made for speed and science during the twin missions' nearly 50-year journey, specifically during the first bit when they were flying by planets. The result is Voyager 1 is zooming out at a speed of 3.5 Earth-sun distances (astronomical units a year), while Voyager 2 has a more stately speed of 3.1 Earth-sun distances, according to NASA.

title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day From Earth

author: BeauHD
description:
Artion Kurtaj, the British hacker responsible for leaking early footage of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022, pleaded guilty Monday to six offenses stemming from cyberattacks against Rockstar Games, Uber and Revolut. The 21-year-old, who was previously deemed unfit to stand trial due to severe autism, carried out the hacking spree "using a mobile phone and an Amazon Fire Stick connected to a hotel room television," reports The Record, "despite bail restrictions limiting his access to the internet." From the report: Now 21, he admitted six offenses at Woolwich Crown Court on Monday, four under the Computer Misuse Act, one of fraud and one of possession of a mobile phone in prison, and is due to be sentenced next week. Kurtaj "used sophisticated hacking techniques to carry out a sustained campaign of cyberattacks, causing serious disruption to major international business and putting sensitive information at risk," said specialist prosecutor Robert Hutchinson.

title: Hacker Pleads Guilty to Leak of Grand Theft Auto VI Footage

author: BeauHD
description: An anonymous reader quotes a report from The Hill: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) confirmed Tuesday that it was withdrawing the U.S.'s measles elimination status, ending more than two decades of what is considered to be one of the greatest public health achievements in modern history. The U.S. met with PAHO's Measles and Rubella Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission for a three-day, closed-door meeting last week. "The commission concluded that the endemic measles transmission has now been reestablished in Bolivia, Mexico and the United States, and recommended that their measles elimination status be withdrawn, a recommendation which I have accepted," Jarbas Barbosa, PAHO's director, said during the briefing Tuesday. The U.S. achieved measles elimination status in 2000 and has held onto that for more than 25 years. But the past two years have seen close to 8,000 measles infections and roughly a dozen related deaths. This year has been the worst in
title: US Officially a Measles Endemic Country

author: BeauHD
description:
Nvidia's board has unanimously rejected former CEO Jensen Huang's offer to return, despite public support from President Trump and prominent Silicon Valley figures. The decision came as Nvidia reported blockbuster third-quarter revenue of $116 billion, double the year-earlier figure. The Associated Press reports: The embattled company's board of directors "unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones said at the start of Nvidia's quarterly earnings call before yielding to Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who is running the company as a permanent replacement is sought. [...] Earlier on Tuesday, Huang said in a social media post that if the board decided that his return was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company and the country, he would be "honored to answer these calls." He acknowledged making "serious mistakes" in his personal life.
 
The turmoil notwithstanding, Nvidia blew past Wall St
title: Nvidia Rejects Jensen Huang's Offer to Return as CEO
